### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 each ran in roughly a third of traces (about 37, 31 and 35 in 100 — 73, 62 and 70 of 200 traces, at most once per trace); in the later window they have practically disappeared, with A19 in 1 of 200 traces and A20 and A25 in none. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- Earlier, these three were alternative intermediate steps between A41 and A26: about 86 in 100 of A41's outgoing transitions led to one of them (A19 about 29, A20 about 26, A25 about 32 in 100), and each of the three in turn led to A26 in about 94–97 in 100 of its outgoing transitions. In the later window, about 86 in 100 of A41's outgoing transitions lead straight to A26. [DIR005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004]
- The A41–A26 distance shortened accordingly: earlier, A26 followed A41 two positions later in about 85 in 100 traces (three positions in about 15 in 100); in the later window it immediately follows A41 in about 86 in 100 traces. [LAG001]
- The relations changed accordingly: earlier, every observed execution of A19, A20 or A25 co-occurred with A26 (about 31–37 in 100 traces per pair) and A41 always ran before them; in the later window A26, A31 and A41 occur without them in essentially all traces (about 100 in 100). [REL004, REL009, REL013, REL005, REL010, REL014, REL006, REL011, REL015]
- Earlier, the three were nearly mutually exclusive alternatives — each pair co-occurred in only about 1 in 100 traces while each ran alone in about 30–36 in 100 — whereas in the later window no pair of them co-occurs; A24, which previously co-occurred with A19 or A20 in about 17 in 100 traces, now typically appears alone (about 56 in 100). [REL001, REL003, REL008, REL002, REL007, REL012]
- Separately, the successor shares of A21 shifted: A24 rose from about 14 to about 35 in 100 of A21's outgoing transitions, while A31 fell from about 54 to about 38 in 100 and A23 from about 29 to about 25 in 100, with both well observed in both windows. [DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the intermediate step between A41 and A26 — previously carried out by one of the alternative activities A19, A20 or A25 — is no longer executed, so that in the later window A41 connects directly to A26. Earlier, about 86 in 100 A41 executions continued into one of the three, each of which led to A26 in about 95 in 100 cases, and A26 followed A41 two positions later in about 85 in 100 traces; in the later window A41 leads directly to A26 in about 86 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, A26 immediately follows A41 in about 86 in 100 traces, and A19, A20 and A25 appear in at most 1 of 200 traces. The change is shown directly by the participation, successor, relation and distance indicators and is consistent across them, and the 24 qualifying items far exceed the fewer than one item expected by chance for an unchanged process [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, REL004, REL009, REL013, LAG001]. Because the three activities are nearly absent in the later window, this is a disappearance or bypass of a process segment, not a shift of shares between surviving paths.

The evidence cannot distinguish a permanent removal from the segment being skipped in every observed case, since zero participation only means the activities were not observed; it also cannot rule out that another activity took over their role, although the immediate A41–A26 succession argues against an intermediate replacement. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, LAG001]

Other differences: at A21, the outgoing shares redistributed towards A24 (from about 14 to about 35 in 100) at the expense of A31 (from about 54 to about 38 in 100); the evidence does not show whether this is connected to the disappearance of A19, A20 and A25. [DIR003]
